objective: Implement a strict, bounded, one-attempt sidecar WebSocket presence client core that consumes one realtime ticket and translates the accepted cloud presence lifecycle into typed owner events without yet wiring launcher control or the ROM bridge loop.
closed_decisions: This checkpoint adds a standalone realtime client core and public owner/driver seam only; it does not modify LocalSidecar, control messages, launcher code, CLI arguments, ROM/Lua code, or any protocol version.

RealtimeGrant owns a non-Clone RealtimeTicket, a validated endpoint, and a nonzero expiry. It exposes no ticket getter, serialization, request replay, peer close reason, or secret-bearing Debug/Display output.

Endpoint text is UTF-8 bounded to 256 bytes, canonical, has exact path /v1/realtime, and has no credentials, query, or fragment. Plain ws requires literal loopback and an explicit nonzero port. Secure wss may use a canonical DNS/IP host and its explicit or default TLS port so the API is not local-only.
One run consumes one grant and makes at most one WebSocket upgrade attempt with exactly one Authorization Bearer ticket, no query ticket, and no subprotocol. It never reconnects or retries a ticket.
The core receives one valid cached LocalPresenceStateV1 at channel construction and sends it as the first application frame immediately after upgrade, within bounded connect/write/ready deadlines.

Latest local player state uses latest-value coalescing and transmits at most once per 100 ms tick. Interactions use a bounded FIFO, are accepted only after readiness, receive one write attempt, and are never replayed after failure.

Only strict coop-cloud encoders/decoders are used. Inbound application data is text-only, assembled messages and frames are capped at 2048 bytes, and exactly one PresenceReady must precede lifecycle events.

Track at most four non-self remote handles. Reject duplicate spawn, update or despawn before spawn, non-newer lifecycle sequences, unknown handles, self events, repeated readiness, binary data, malformed text, and lifecycle capacity overflow.

The realtime task returns stable redacted outcomes. Owner event backpressure terminates the task rather than growing memory; owner stop/drop, peer close, expiry, timeout, protocol, transport, and capacity conditions remain distinguishable without remote-controlled text.
The single LocalSidecar bridge writer remains the future owner of bridge framing and outer sidecar sequence allocation; this module emits typed presence values only and never writes ROM TCP frames.
forbidden_changes: Do not edit coop-sidecar server.rs, control.rs, main.rs, launcher/server/ROM/Lua code, root Cargo.toml, documentation, generated artifacts, or orchestration state.
Do not put tickets in argv, environment, URLs, query strings, logs, Debug/Display output, cloneable values, replay ledgers, unbounded queues, or retry paths.

Do not hand-roll realtime JSON, accept binary application frames, accept lifecycle before readiness, expose peer close reasons, allocate an unbounded buffer, reconnect internally, or let the realtime task write directly to the ROM bridge.
Do not stage, commit, branch, fetch, pull, push, contact repository remotes, create or remove worktrees, or revert another worker's edits. Test loopback networking is authorized.

acceptance_criteria.description: RealtimeGrant and endpoint validation enforce all scheme, origin, path, canonicality, length, credential/query/fragment, nonzero-port, expiry, and maximum-ticket-TTL boundaries while keeping the ticket non-Clone, non-serializable, and redacted.

A deterministic loopback server observes one header-only bearer ticket, no subprotocol or query, and the exact cached PLAYER_STATE as the first application frame; connect, write, and readiness waits are bounded.
After one valid PRESENCE_READY, latest player states are coalesced to at most 10 Hz and bounded FIFO interactions are written once in order and discarded on write failure.

Strict server text decoding yields typed Ready, Spawn, Update, and Despawn owner events in order while enforcing readiness, self-handle, four-remote capacity, handle lifecycle, and RFC 1982 server-sequence invariants.

Oversized, binary, malformed, repeated-ready, lifecycle-before-ready, unknown-handle, stale/equal/half-range, peer-close, timeout, owner-stop/drop, and output-backpressure cases return only stable redacted outcomes without leaking ticket or peer-controlled close text.
Focused and full coop-sidecar tests, strict Clippy, formatting, and diff checks pass with all changes confined to the owned files and no production integration falsely claimed.

return_when: Every acceptance criterion is resolved and all verification outcomes are recorded.
A safe one-attempt API cannot be implemented without changing a forbidden launcher, control, bridge-loop, or protocol boundary.
A concrete dependency, toolchain, or isolated-worktree failure prevents progress within the execution budget.
